analyses within tobacco groups were unstable or could not be estimated because too few men used cannabis without tobacco: in the paper's supplementary table, the 678 men who reported using cannabis but no tobacco had one lung cancer between them (in the 216 who had used cannabis once), so no hazard ratio could be estimated for men who had used cannabis more than once without tobacco.

evidence_add.locator: Supplemental Table 1, rows with tobacco 'Never' and cannabis once, 2–4, 5–10, 11–50 and more than 50 times
evidence_add.extracted: Supplemental Table 1 (44,257 conscripts with all covariates; 179 lung cancer outcomes), combined cannabis and tobacco exposure: men reporting cannabis use and no tobacco numbered 216 (once; 1 lung cancer; adjusted HR 3.14, 95% CI 0.42–23.10), 214 (2–4 times; 0), 100 (5–10 times; 0), 88 (11–50 times; 0) and 60 (more than 50 times; 0), against 17,700 men who used neither (29 lung cancers; reference). No hazard ratio is given for the groups with no lung cancer.

change: The paper's supplement (saved by the senior author on 25 October) read in full: among men who used cannabis but not tobacco there was one lung cancer, so cannabis without tobacco could not be studied. The statement now says so with the counts; the conclusion and the certainty are unchanged.
